title: Relational Invariant Learning for Robust Solvation Free Energy Prediction

source_version.publication: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR volume 267 (2025)
source_version.version_basis: official publisher linked PDF acquired on retrieval date, frozen by SHA-256

inspection_outcome: Three demonstrated core mathematical failures and one unresolved empirical result-binding concern
summary: The published variational identity/objective, contrastive mechanism, and mixup risk upper bound fail independent checks. Each supports a named core module. Missing implementation and raw runs prevent conclusions about which equations generated the published scores.

problems.title: Invalid variational identity and inconsistent minimized loss signs
problems.claim: Equations5–6 and21–24 derive MCVAE from conditional evidence and regularize toward a prior
assumptions: Constant environment, normalized Gaussian joint with positive variances
Literal Eq23 counterexample uses q equal to true posterior, satisfying every positive KL threshold
Sign diagnostic explicitly separates reconstruction variance1 from posterior variancev
problems.check: Parent analytic Gaussian decomposition, symbolic exact values, charitable prior correction and finite delta0.4 comparison
problems.result: Literal RHS exceeds log evidence by0.0965735903; intended prior version still omits posterior gap; negativeKL plus positive reconstruction reverses the correct sign
problems.counterevidence: Prose mentions correct environment-conditioned prior; corrected prior gives a valid lower bound but not claimed equality; tied variance interpretation limits unboundedness diagnosis; actual training code absent
problems.impact: Invalid mathematical basis for core MCVAE and Proposition4.2; historical divergence or benchmark loss not established

correction.statement: Use coherent conditional prior and full ELBO decomposition; minimize negative log likelihood plus positive KL
correction.limits: Does not prove sufficiency/OOD invariance; no neural rerun; exact decoder/variance binding needed

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: Eq.23 literally uses a data-conditional posterior in the KL and claims an evidence equality. In the normalized Gaussian example with q equal to the true posterior, the claimed right side exceeds log evidence by (log 2)/2-1/4. Even the more favorable prior interpretation needs the posterior-KL gap. The negative KL and positive reconstruction terms are then explicitly minimized.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: The report distinguishes posterior from decoder variance and does not rely solely on a tied-variance interpretation. A conventional ELBO with the correct gap/signs would be a different expression.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Major is retained because this invalid variational identity/sign mechanism directly enters the core objective and Proposition 4.2 dependency.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The report's corrected variational identity is local; it does not claim to have rederived every downstream guarantee or rerun the model.

problems.title: Matched-pair denominator does not implement contrastive discrimination
problems.claim: Eq12 approximates the mutual-information objective of Eq11
assumptions: Printed denominator contains matched j,j scores
Nonzero unit vectors for dot-product or cosine demonstration
problems.check: Exact log-sum-exp reduction and Jensen proof; constant versus informative finite representations; gradient at equal scores
problems.result: Loss>=logM with equality at any equal matched scores, including zero-MI collapse; no anchor-negative discrimination
problems.counterevidence: Supervised term may prevent overall model collapse; an intended corrected index is plausible but not evidenced by code or appendix
problems.impact: Central MI/invariance mechanism is mathematically unsupported as published; no benchmark loss required for this assessment

correction.statement: Compare each anchor to mismatched samples and specify conditioning/negative distribution
correction.limits: Index repair alone does not establish conditional-MI bound or OOD invariance

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: Eq.12 uses matched j,j scores in the denominator. It reduces to log(sum exp(s_j))-mean(s_i), whose minimum log M requires only equal matched scores. Both a constant nonzero unit representation and an informative representation attain it while having different mutual information.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: A supervised term may prevent whole-network collapse. This does not restore the claimed contrastive discrimination or mutual-information interpretation of this term.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Major is retained for the invalid core MI mechanism without requiring proof that the entire predictor collapses.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: Changing negative-pair indexing is a candidate local correction; a conditional-MI guarantee is not asserted without a separate proof.

problems.title: Nuisance-information upper bound fails on admissible bounded regression
problems.claim: Eq19 and Eq20 upper-bound mixup error by optimal risk plus nuisance mutual information
problems.check: Parent exact expected risk and mutual independence; optimal clip/projection predictor witnesses zero attainable risk
problems.result: Actual risk1/4, RHS0 for every c2; every stated A1 hypothesis satisfied
problems.counterevidence: No optimizer assumption is stated; adding it changes the claim; qualitative mixup intuition can survive
problems.impact: The explicitly invoked theoretical justification of mixup MCVAE is false under its stated assumptions

correction.statement: A valid replacement needs additional assumptions and an excess-risk/approximation term
correction.limits: No general corrected theorem or empirical change established

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: A.1 assumes a Lipschitz predictor and bounded nonnegative loss but not optimal training. With fair-bit Y, informative H1=H2, independent nuisance, and constant predictor 1/2, nuisance MI is zero, optimal risk is zero, and actual risk is 1/4. The predictor satisfies the stated Lipschitz upper bound; the one-hot encoding variant is also admissible.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: No hidden optimality assumption appears in the checked statement. Additional approximation/optimization terms could change a repaired theorem, but are absent from the printed bound.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Major is retained because the source explicitly uses this theorem to justify its core mixup mechanism. Appendix placement does not diminish that dependency.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The report identifies required missing assumptions or residual terms without presenting an unproved universal repaired bound.

problems.title: CompSolv solvent score and sensitivity runs lack consistent bindings
problems.outcome: Material reporting conflict with unresolved historical value
problems.claim: Full RILOOD achieves best OOD score under the reported CompSolv solvent protocol
assumptions: Cross-table ranking comparison is conditional on same protocol
problems.check: Parent original images, complete protocol reading, exact displayed score difference
problems.result: 0.3660±.022 versus0.4689±.006; latter would lose to two displayed baselines if comparable; figure labels/grids unresolved
problems.counterevidence: Different configurations or transcription error could explain conflict; Table1 shows six lowest RILOOD means; other shared cells agree; no raw run identifies correct entry
problems.impact: Cannot independently confirm this ranking or correct a score; not proof all experiments fail

correction.statement: Provide split/configuration/seed/prediction mappings to both tables and sensitivity plots
correction.limits: No raw datasets or predictions acquired

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: The shared CompSolv solvent cell is 0.3660 +/- 0.022 in Table 1 and 0.4689 +/- 0.006 in Table 2, a difference of 0.1029, while the other three corresponding cells agree. The displayed sensitivity grids and prose grids also differ by a factor of ten.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: Different configurations or runs could explain the values. The source does not identify a unique corrected historical score or parameter grid.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Needs Evidence is retained for unresolved run/configuration bindings. Conditional baseline comparisons are not represented as a verified rank reversal.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: No score is replaced; exact run IDs, settings, and grid-to-figure bindings are needed.

clarifications: Graph-level feature interpretation resolves apparent mixup atom-count incompatibility
A3 marginal invariance does not itself prove label-conditional invariance; XOR example demonstrates the distinction
Eq11 conditional-information maximization can preserve nuisance information
Table2 without-MCAR does not beat its baseline on both scaffold columns
FreeSolv comparator named CGIB in prose is actually CMRL in Table4
Validation checkpoint selection is stated; test sensitivity plots alone do not prove test-set tuning
Table4 extensions are IID and include additional property tasks; intended solvent/scaffold group disjointness is a positive safeguard

unresolved_claims.reason: Listed marginal/factorization conditions and unrestricted residual noise do not supply that bridge
